qs.q: The atlas (C1 vertebra) features a transverse foramen that transmits a major cranial-bound vessel. What is the primary structure traversing this foramen?
qs.e: The vertebral artery is the main structure traversing the transverse foramen of the atlas. The internal jugular vein exits through the jugular foramen in the skull base.
qs.s: Review — Skin, Embryology, Spine & Skull: MCQs

qs.q: During a routine radiological examination of the cervical spine, a structure passing through the transverse foramen of the atlas (C1 vertebra) is evaluated. What is this main structure?
qs.e: The vertebral artery is the main structure traversing the transverse foramen of the atlas. The internal jugular vein and common carotid artery do not pass through this foramen.
qs.s: Review — Skin, Embryology, Spine & Skull: MCQs

qs.q: During dissection of the posterior cranial region, the posterior tubercle and arch region of the atlas are examined for ligamentous attachments. Which specific ligament attaches at this region?
qs.e: The apical ligament of the dens attaches at the posterior tubercle and arch region along with the posterior atlanto-occipital membrane region. Other ligaments such as the tectorial membrane have different attachment sites.
qs.s: Review — Skin, Embryology, Spine & Skull: MCQs
